headline: Presented alternatives for the Adelphia Cable Pond Retrofit; Green Community Festival preparations discussed.
summary: Fuss & O'Neill presented alternatives for the Adelphia Cable Pond Retrofit to help reduce phosphorus runoff and control water flow into Potash Brook. The storm water permit will come up for renewal, and the presenters hope the property owner will work with the city. Members also discussed plans for the Green Community Festival on Sept 19, 2026, and unanimously adopted the prior meeting minutes.
decisions: Adopted the meeting minutes from 15, 2026 unanimously.

plain_text:
NATURAL RESOURCES & CONSERV ATION COMMITTEE 
Meeting Minutes 
August 05, 2026 
 
The South Burlington NRCC held it's regular monthly meeting for August 05, 2026, at 6:00 pm, in 
room 301 at the South Burlington City Hall, 180 Market St, and by GoToMeeting for remote 
participation. 
 
Attending: J. Bossange (Vice Chr); J. Hunt; L. Yankowski; K. Boyk; G. Leckey; M. Huth; 
 
Also attending:  S. Kershner (City Liaison); L. Smith ( City Council Liaison); B. McCreavy (SB Dpty 
Director of Water Resources); C. Foley (SB Storm water Project Mgr.); Jacob Fowler & John Arkbella 
(Fuss & O'Neill, for the Adelphia Cable Pond Retrofit);  R. Doyle 
 
1. Mr Bossange welcomed everyone. 
2. No changes, deletions or additions to the agenda. 
3. Meeting minutes from  15, 2026. 
1. Ms Boyk motioned to adopt, Ms Yankowski 2nd.  Adopted unanimously. 
4. Comments from the public. 
1. Ms Yankowski wanted to remind everyone that the Primary Elections are Tuesday August 
11, 2026.  It is important to vote .  South Burlington has a big decision to make about the 
Bartlett Bay Treatment Center.  Mr Smith mention the State of VT had a vote that reduced 
wetland setbacks by 25 ft.  This is despite flooding issues over the last few years. Mr 
Bossange asked if the 100ft set back South Burlington adopted will be affected.  Ms 
Yankowski believes not from past discussions about about city and state regulations. 
5. Adelphia Cable Pond Retrofit- Alternatives presentation 
1. Presented by  Jacob Fowler & John Arkbella (Fuss & O'Neill).  Ref: 4673 .  The storm water 
permit will be coming up for renewal and it is hoped the property owner will work with the 
city.  The designs are to help mitigate phosphorus runoff and control water flow into Potash 
Brook. 
6. Green Community Festival 
1. Ms Yankowski had to let the committee know VINS (VT Institute of Natural Science) will 
not be able to attend with any of their birds.  Ms Leckey and Mr Bossange are working on 
the Mission Statement.  Ms Hunt is working on possible wildlife at the event.  Ms Boyk has 
a watershed model she will see if it is possible to use at the festival.  Ms Balerna is working 
on rewilding. 
2. We have more work to get ready and should review what we have at our next meeting. 
7. Member updates and reports 
1. No new updates. 
8. Other business and agenda planning. 
1. The Open Space Advisory Group, (MS Boyk is our representative), did meet.  The 
consultants- Civic Sol, have been working on their process for tying goals to a budget for 
the city.  Mr Smith sent a link to the presentation for the committee to look at.  We will get 
an actual presentation from Civic Sol and the preliminary plans will be presented to the 
public at a later date.  Their work involves addressing the overall needs of the city. 
 
Our next meeting is September 09, 2026 at 6pm.  Green Community Festival is Sept 
 19, 2026
